mainTopic: Vows a husband imposes on his wife, and wives who lose their כתובה for breaking דת משה or דת יהודית
overview: The amud opens by finishing an explanation from before. A husband who stops his wife from visiting mourners is cutting her off, because if she never comforts others, no one will mourn her. רבי מאיר supports this from a פסוק in קהלת. The גמרא then explains other lines of the משנה. The husband's 'other reason' must be a real, well-known worry about immoral people. Saying 'shameful words' or doing a pointless chore that makes her look foolish are real harms, so she may leave with her כתובה. רב כהנא and a ברייתא add that stopping her from lending household tools ruins her name with the neighbors. A new משנה then lists wives who lose their כתובה for breaking דת משה or דת יהודית. The גמרא explains how a husband can find out about each דת משה case and why unkept vows matter. The חכמים reject the idea that he should simply keep fixing her wrongs himself. Finally, the גמרא asks why an uncovered head counts only as custom when it is a Torah law, and its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How does banning a house of mourning hurt her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that banning a בית המשתה cuts her off from joy. But it asks how banning a בית האבל 'locks a door' on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a house of feasting, there is a door being locked in front of her. But with a house of mourning, what door is being locked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question it started just before. Keeping her from a party clearly takes away her happiness, but keeping her from mourners seems to take nothing from her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats both bans the same and calls both 'locking a door in front of her.' Going to a mourner's house is not fun, so it seems she loses nothing. The גמרא needs to show what she really loses.

keyTerms.meaning: Locking [a door] in front of her, meaning cutting her off from something
A house of mourning, where people come to comfort mourners

phrases.english: [with a house of feasting] there is locking [a door] in front of her,
but [banning her from going] to a house of mourning,
what locking in front of her is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְבֵית הָאֵבֶל מַאי נוֹעֵל בְּפָנֶיהָ אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question from before this section, about how the משנה's wording fits both cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that banning a בית האבל counts as 'locking a door in front of her.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Visiting mourners brings her no pleasure, so taking it away does not seem to cut her off from anything.

steps.title: No one will eulogize her
steps.stepSummary: A תנא explains that if she never mourns others, one day no one will mourn her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Tomorrow she will die, and no one will eulogize her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Missing out on comforting others hurts her later, because when she dies, no one will come to mourn for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loss is not today but in the future. People treat you the way you treated them. A woman who never shows up for others' losses will have no one show up at her own death.

phrases.english: It was taught:
tomorrow she will die,
phrases.notes: 'Tomorrow' here just means 'someday in the future.'

phrases.english: and no person will eulogize her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does she lose by not going to a בית האבל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the future no one will eulogize her, so she really is being cut off.

steps.title: Another version: no one will care about her
steps.stepSummary: A different version of the same teaching says no one will value or pay attention to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: no person will value her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way the teaching was said. It changes one word from 'eulogize her' to 'value her.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the harm is wider than her funeral. A person who never shows up for others cuts herself off, and people stop caring about her. Both versions agree that banning the בית האבל really does hurt her.

keyTerms.meaning: Values her, pays attention to her

phrases.english: And some say:
no person will value her.
phrases.notes: סופנה (values her) looks almost the same as סופדה (eulogizes her), and the גמרא swaps one for the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֵין כׇּל בְּרִיָּה סוֹפְנָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the answer in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does she lose by not going to a בית האבל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People will not value or pay attention to her.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: those who honor the dead will be honored
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי מאיר explains a פסוק in קהלת: whatever you do for the dead, others will do for you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר used to say: What does the verse mean, 'It is better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of feasting, since that is the end of all men, and the living will take it to heart'? What does 'the living will take it to heart' mean? Matters of death: whoever eulogizes will be eulogized, whoever buries will be buried, whoever lifts [the dead] will be lifted, whoever escorts will be escorted, whoever carries will be carried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the idea from step 2. What you do for others at a death is what will be done for you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר reads 'the living will take it to heart' as a lesson: the living should realize that their own funeral will match how they treated others. This backs up the claim that a woman kept from the בית האבל loses something real.

keyTerms.meaning: A house of feasting, a party or celebration
And the living will take it to heart

steps.whatToRemember: Visiting mourners is not a 'nothing.' The way you treat others at their loss is the way you will be treated, so a husband who bans it really is cutting his wife off.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say:
What is [the meaning of] that which is written:
'It is better to go to a house of mourning
than to go to a house of feasting,
since that is the end of all men,
and the living will take it to heart'?
What does 'and the living will take it to heart' mean?
Matters of death:
one who eulogizes, they will eulogize him;
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets here and in the next lines are added in the corrected wording. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: one who buries, they will bury him;
one who lifts [the dead], they will lift him;
one who escorts, they will escort him;
one who carries, they will carry him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that someone who does not mourn others will not be mourned.

steps.title: What is the husband's 'other reason'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if the husband bans her for some other reason, he may. It asks what that other reason is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he claimed it was because of something else, he is allowed. What is 'something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה. It asks what kind of 'other reason' lets the husband keep her away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the husband who bans the בית האבל or the בית המשתה must divorce her and pay the כתובה. But if he has a different motive, he is permitted to ban it. The גמרא wants to know exactly what motive counts.

phrases.english: And if he claimed [that he banned her]
because of something else, he is permitted.
What is 'something else'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיָה טוֹעֵן מִשּׁוּם דָּבָר אַחֵר רַשַּׁאי. מַאי דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'other reason' allows the husband to keep her from these places?

steps.title: Worry about immoral people there
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the reason is that immoral people are often found there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Because of immoral people who are commonly found there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'other reason' is the husband's worry that improper, loose people hang around that place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is not about cutting her off. It is about protecting her from a bad crowd. That is why the husband is allowed to keep her away.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Because of immoral people
who are commonly found there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מִשּׁוּם בְּנֵי אָדָם פְּרוּצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Immoral people are commonly found at that place.

steps.title: Only if the place is known for it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits the rule: the husband's claim works only if that place is already known to have such people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We only said this where it is established [that such people are there]. But if it is not established, it is not in his power.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to שמואל's answer. The husband cannot just make up this excuse; the place must already have a known reputation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this limit, any husband could claim 'bad people are there' and escape the משנה's rule. רב אשי requires a חזקה, an established fact, that such people really are there.

keyTerms.meaning: It was established, has a known reputation
It is not in his power

steps.whyThisMatters: It stops the husband's 'other reason' from becoming an easy loophole. His claim must match known reality.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We only said this where it is established [that such people are there],
but if it is not established,
it is not in his power [to claim it].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּאִיתַּחְזַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband may use the 'immoral people' reason only if the place is known to have them; otherwise his claim does not help.

steps.title: Why can't she just say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a vow 'on condition that you say' something, and asks why she doesn't just say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If he said to her, '[The vow is cancelled] on condition that you say [certain words].' Let her say it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line in the משנה. It challenges why the husband must divorce her if she could simply say the words and be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says this condition forces him to divorce her and pay the כתובה. But saying a few words seems easy, so why is it treated as harming her? The גמרא is challenging the משנה's ruling.

phrases.english: And if he said to her
'on condition that you say [certain words].'
phrases.notes: The משנה means: say to someone else what you told me, or what I told you.

phrases.english: So let her say it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לָהּ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתֹּאמְרִי. וְתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that this condition forces divorce with a כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeating some words is easy, so the condition does not seem to harm her.

steps.title: They are shameful words
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the words are degrading, private matters she would be ashamed to repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: [These are] shameful matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words are shameful and private, so making her say them in front of others really does hurt her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition is not about any words. It is about private, intimate talk between husband and wife, and saying it to others would shame her. That is why the משנה treats it as grounds for divorce with a כתובה.
steps.whatToRemember: A husband's vow or condition that shames or isolates his wife lets her leave the marriage with her כתובה, unless he has a real, recognized reason.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
[These are] shameful matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: דְּבָרִים שֶׁל קָלוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words might be ordinary words that are easy to say.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words are shameful private matters, so the condition truly harms her.

steps.title: Why can't she just fill and pour out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a vow 'on condition that she fill and pour out onto the garbage heap' and asks why she doesn't simply do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Or that she should fill and pour out onto the garbage heap.' So let her just do it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה and challenges it: filling and pouring out sounds harmless, so why should this let her leave with her כתובה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge has the same shape as Step 8. If the condition is easy, she can meet it and the vow goes away, so the husband hasn't really harmed her. The גמרא wants to know what is so hard about it.

phrases.english: Or that she should fill
and pour out onto the garbage heap.
So let her do it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as Step 8, now aimed at the next case in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the condition 'fill and pour out' lets her leave with her כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Filling and pouring out seems easy, so she could meet the condition and lose nothing.

steps.title: שמואל: it is a polite way of describing preventing pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that 'fill and pour out' really means 'fill and shake out' after relations, a polite way of saying she must prevent pregnancy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it means that she should fill and then shake out.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the משנה is speaking in polite language about married relations, not about water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the husband wants her to prevent herself from becoming pregnant. That is a serious harm to her, so of course she does not have to agree, and she may leave with her כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture buckets of water here. שמואל understands 'fill' and 'shake out' as a polite way of speaking about married relations.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
That she should fill and shake out.
phrases.notes: He means after relations: she would shake out the seed so she doesn't become pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: the words are a polite way of describing preventing pregnancy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition is a simple, harmless chore with water.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition means preventing pregnancy, which she may refuse.

steps.title: The ברייתא: pouring ten jugs of water into the garbage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the case literally: she must fill ten jugs of water and pour them onto the garbage heap.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: that she should fill ten jugs of water and pour them onto the garbage heap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, different explanation from a ברייתא, which reads the words in their plain sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the husband really is asking for a pointless chore with water. This explains the case differently from שמואל, and the next step questions whether it truly answers the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: in a ברייתא it was taught

phrases.english: In a baraita it was taught:
that she should fill ten jugs of water
and pour them onto the garbage heap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different explanation of the case from the one שמואל gave
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is literally a pointless chore with water.

steps.title: According to the ברייתא, what is the harm?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's reading clearly justifies divorce with a כתובה, but by the ברייתא's reading the chore seems harmless, so why shouldn't she just do it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to שמואל: that is why he must divorce her and pay her כתובה. But according to the ברייתא, what difference does it make to her? Let her do it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two explanations. It accepts שמואל's reading but challenges the ברייתא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Preventing pregnancy is clearly a real harm. Pouring out ten jugs of water costs her only a little effort, so the original challenge from Step 10 seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense (according to one view, but not the other)
what difference does it make to her?
he must divorce her and pay her כתובה

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Shmuel:
for that reason he must divorce her
and pay her ketubah.
But according to the baraita,
what difference does it make to her?
Let her do it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's explanation from Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's reading of the case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A pointless chore does her no real harm, so it should not be grounds for divorce with a כתובה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: she would look like a fool
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן answers that doing such a pointless act makes her look crazy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: because she looks like a fool.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends the ברייתא: the harm is not the effort but the embarrassment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring good water into the garbage for no reason makes people think she is not in her right mind. A wife does not have to accept being made to look foolish, so she may leave with her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: a fool or a crazy person

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of 'fill and pour out.' שמואל: preventing pregnancy. The ברייתא: a pointless chore, which counts as harm because it makes her look like a fool.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Because she looks like a fool.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a different kind of harm: shame, not effort
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only possible harm is the effort, which is small.
steps.terutzMaskana: Looking foolish in public is a real harm.

steps.title: רב כהנא: forbidding her to borrow or lend household tools
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that a husband who forbids his wife by vow to borrow or lend common household tools must divorce her and pay her כתובה, because he gives her a bad name among her neighbors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: one who forbids his wife by vow to borrow or lend a sifter, a sieve, a mill, or an oven must divorce her and pay her כתובה, because he gives her a bad name among her neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב כהנא, adding another vow to the list of those that force the husband to divorce her and pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neighbors normally lend these tools to one another. If she suddenly stops, they will think she is stingy or stuck-up. The harm is to her reputation.

keyTerms.meaning: one who forbids someone by a vow
a fine sifter and a coarse sieve

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
One who forbids his wife by a vow
that she may not borrow and may not lend
a sifter, a sieve, a mill, or an oven
must divorce her and pay her ketubah,
because he gives her a bad name among her neighbors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new vow, not in the משנה, that is also grounds for divorce with a כתובה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow forbidding her to borrow or lend household tools forces him to divorce her and pay her כתובה, because it damages her reputation.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב כהנא and adds the reverse case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches רב כהנא's ruling word for word. It adds that if the wife makes such a vow, or vows not to weave nice clothes for his children, she can be divorced without her כתובה, because she gives him a bad name.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: one who forbids his wife by vow to borrow or lend a sifter, a sieve, a mill, or an oven must divorce her and pay her כתובה, because he gives her a bad name among her neighbors. Similarly, if she vowed not to borrow or lend these, or not to weave nice clothes for his children, she leaves without her כתובה, because she gives him a bad name among his neighbors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב כהנא's ruling and also teaches the same idea in reverse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא matches רב כהנא exactly. The second half shows the rule works both ways: if she is the one who damages his name, she loses her כתובה. Neighbors would assume he told her to act this way.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this (support for the last statement)

steps.whatToRemember: Damaging your spouse's reputation in the neighborhood is a real harm. If the husband does it, he pays her כתובה. If the wife does it, she loses her כתובה.

phrases.english: A baraita also teaches this:
One who forbids his wife by a vow
that she may not borrow and may not lend
a sifter, a sieve, a mill, or an oven
must divorce her and pay her ketubah,
because he gives her a bad name among her neighbors.
And similarly, if she is the one who vowed
not to borrow and not to lend
a sifter, a sieve, a mill, or an oven,
or not to weave nice clothes for his children,
she leaves without her ketubah,
because she gives him a bad name among his neighbors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא from Step 15 and adds the reverse case
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's ruling about forbidding her to borrow or lend tools
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same ruling, plus the parallel case of a wife's vow

steps.title: The new משנה: women who lose their כתובה for breaking דת משה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a woman who breaks דת משה or דת יהודית is divorced without a כתובה, and lists the cases of דת משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These women are divorced without their כתובה: one who breaks the law of משה or the Jewish custom. What counts as breaking the law of משה? She feeds him untithed food, she is with him while a נדה, she does not separate חלה, or she makes vows and doesn't keep them.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה begins. It lists women who can be divorced without receiving their כתובה money and starts with the Torah-law cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two groups: דת משה, which means real Torah laws, and דת יהודית, which means the modest conduct Jewish women accept. In the first three דת משה cases (food, family purity, חלה), the wife causes her husband to sin through things he relies on her for. In the vows case only she sins, and step 28 explains why it still affects him.

keyTerms.meaning: The money a husband promises his wife if he divorces her or dies
The law of משה, meaning Torah law
Food from which מעשרות (tithes) have been taken
A woman in her menstrual status, forbidden to her husband
A portion of dough that must be separated for the כהן

phrases.english: MISHNA: And these are divorced without a marriage contract payment:
one who violates the law of Moshe or the Jewish custom.
And what is the law of Moshe?
She feeds him untithed food,
or she has relations with him while a menstruating woman,
or she does not separate חלה from the dough,
or she makes vows and does not fulfill them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the earlier discussion of a husband's vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who breaks דת משה (untithed food, נדה, חלה, broken vows) may be divorced without her כתובה.

steps.title: The משנה lists the cases of דת יהודית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines דת יהודית: going out with uncovered hair, spinning in the marketplace, and chatting with every man.
steps.simpleTranslation: What counts as breaking the Jewish custom? She goes out with her hair uncovered, she spins wool in the marketplace, or she talks freely with every man.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and gives the second group: acts against the accepted modesty of Jewish women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not the same type as the דת משה cases. They are about public behavior that breaks basic standards of modesty, and they also cost her the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: The accepted modest conduct of Jewish women
Spins wool in the public marketplace

phrases.english: And what is the Jewish custom?
She goes out with her head uncovered,
or she spins in the marketplace,
or she speaks with every man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the second category named in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out with uncovered hair, spinning in the market, or talking with every man breaks דת יהודית.

steps.title: אבא שאול and רבי טרפון add more cases
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול adds a wife who curses her husband's parents in front of him. רבי טרפון adds a loud woman, whose voice the neighbors hear from inside her house.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: also a woman who curses his parents in front of him. רבי טרפון says: also a loud woman. Who is a loud woman? One who speaks inside her house and her neighbors hear her voice.
steps.whatsHappening: Two תנאים add their own cases to the דת יהודית list, and the משנה defines רבי טרפון's term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אף" (also) shows they accept the earlier list and want to add to it. The loud woman is defined carefully: it is not about volume alone. Her voice from inside her own home carries to the neighbors.

keyTerms.meaning: Curses his parents (literally, "those who gave birth to him")
Also: adds a case on top of the earlier list

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמְקַלֶּלֶת יוֹלְדָיו בְּפָנָיו.
phrases.english: Abba Shaul says: Also one who curses his parents in his presence.
Rabbi Tarfon says: Also a loud woman.
And who is a loud woman?
When she speaks inside her house
and her neighbors hear her voice.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two lists: דת משה (Torah laws, such as untithed food and נדה) and דת יהודית (modest conduct). Breaking either one costs her the כתובה.
steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: אַף הַמְקַלֶּלֶת יוֹלְדָיו בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds further cases to the דת יהודית list from Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא שאול adds cursing his parents in his presence. רבי טרפון adds a loud woman, whose neighbors hear her speaking in her house.

steps.title: How can the untithed-food case happen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the case works. If he knew the food was untithed, he should not have eaten it. If he didn't know, how did he find out?
steps.simpleTranslation: About "she feeds him untithed food": what is the case? If he knows, he should hold back from eating. If he doesn't know, how does he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה's first case. It shows the case seems impossible either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a two-sided trap. If he knew, the sin is his own fault, not hers. If he didn't know, he has no way to prove she did it. Either way, it is unclear how this could be a reason to divorce her without a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does this actually happen?
Let him hold back (and not eat it)

phrases.english: GEMARA: "She feeds him untithed food":
What are the circumstances?
If he knows, he should abstain.
If he does not know, how does he know?
phrases.notes: He means: how could he ever find out afterward that the food was untithed, so as to divorce her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא, questioning the first דת משה case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a wife who feeds her husband untithed food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he knew, she isn't to blame. If he didn't know, he can't prove it. So the case seems unworkable.

steps.title: She lied that a כהן tithed the grain
steps.stepSummary: The case is where she told him a certain כהן fixed the grain pile for her. He asked the כהן and found out it was a lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where she told him: "So-and-so the כהן fixed the pile for me." He went and asked him, and it turned out to be a lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a specific case. He did not know at the time, but he found out later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This escapes both sides of the trap. He wasn't careless, because he relied on her claim. Afterward he has real proof, because the כהן denied it. That shows she knowingly fed him untithed food.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)
Fixed, meaning separated the tithes so the grain may be eaten

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where she said to him: "So-and-so the priest
rectified the grain pile for me,"
and he went and asked him,
and it was found to be a lie.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the husband either knew (so it is his fault) or could never find out.
steps.terutzMaskana: He relied on her claim that a כהן tithed it, then found out from the כהן that she lied.

steps.title: The same problem for the נדה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the נדה case. If he knew, he should have stayed away. If he didn't know, he should be able to rely on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: About "she is with him while a נדה": what is the case? If he knows about her, he should stay away. If he doesn't know, he should be able to rely on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second case and raises a similar problem. This time the second side is different: he is allowed to rely on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the food case the problem was "how can he find out?" Here the problem is stronger. The Torah itself trusts a woman about her נדה status. So if she said she was טהורה, how can he later doubt her and take away her כתובה?

keyTerms.meaning: Let him rely on her (trust what she says)
He knows about her (that she is a נדה)

phrases.english: "Or she has relations with him while a menstruating woman."
What are the circumstances?
If he knows about her, he should abstain;
if he does not know, he should rely on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as Step 20 for the משנה's second case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a wife who is with her husband while a נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he knew, it is his fault. If he didn't know, he is allowed to trust her, so how can he blame her?

steps.title: שמואל's proof that a נדה is trusted for herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up "he should rely on her" with שמואל's teaching from the פסוק "וספרה לה": a נדה counts her days for herself and is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חיננא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: From where do we know that a נדה counts for herself? Because it says "she shall count to herself seven days." "To herself" means by herself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the last line of the question, that he is allowed to rely on her. The question is still open here, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "לה" teaches that the Torah gives her the job of counting her clean days, so her word is trusted. That makes the משנה's case harder. If the Torah trusts her, the husband seems to have no way to prove she was a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: "And she shall count to herself" (the source פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: As Rav Ḥinnana bar Kahana said that Shmuel said:
From where do we know that a menstruating woman counts for herself?
As it is stated: "And she shall count to herself seven days."
"To herself" means by herself!

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's answer. It is proof for the question, showing that the husband really may rely on her. The difficulty is still waiting to be solved.
steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second side of the question in Step 22, that the husband may rely on her.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in Step 22 that a husband may rely on his wife about her נדה status
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's reading of "וספרה לה" (ויקרא 15:28): "לה" means by herself, so she is trusted.

steps.title: She lied that a Sage declared her blood pure
steps.stepSummary: The case is where she told him a חכם declared her blood pure. He checked with the חכם and found out she had lied.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where she told him: 'So-and-so the חכם ruled my blood pure.' He went and asked the חכם, and it turned out to be a lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 22: how could the husband find out about the נדה problem if he was allowed to rely on her? She made a specific claim that he could check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a husband trusts his wife about נדה, so he did nothing wrong by relying on her. But here she named a real person who supposedly ruled for her. Once he asked that חכם, her lie came out, and that is how he learns of it afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)
Declared pure; here, ruled that the blood is not נדה blood

phrases.english: No, it is needed where she said to him:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלוֹנִי חָכָם טִיהֵר לִי אֶת הַדָּם,
phrases.english: So-and-so the Sage declared the blood pure for me,
and he went and asked him, and it turned out to be a lie.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 22, now that step 23 has shown he is allowed to rely on her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he is allowed to rely on her, he could never find out that she misled him.
steps.terutzMaskana: She made a claim he could check (that a named חכם ruled for her), and checking it showed it was a lie.

steps.title: Second answer: her neighbors knew she was a נדה
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the case follows רב יהודה. If her neighbors know she is a נדה, her husband gets מלקות for being with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you like, say it follows רב יהודה, who said: if she is known among her neighbors to be a נדה, her husband gets lashes for being with her because of the נדה prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain how the husband finds out. Her neighbors knew she was a נדה, and he learned it from them afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a husband relies on his wife does not apply when her נדה status is already public among her neighbors. That status counts so strongly that the husband can even get מלקות. So he can discover the truth through the neighbors, and she has misled him.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you prefer, say (introduces another answer)
She was established or known (to have a certain status)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is like Rav Yehuda,
for Rav Yehuda said:
If she was known as a menstruating woman among her neighbors,
her husband is lashed for her on account of נדה.
phrases.notes: So in our case, the neighbors knew, and that is how he finds out later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the same question that step 24 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case setting, based on an outside rule (רב יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A husband always relies on his wife about נדה, so he cannot find out.
steps.terutzMaskana: When her נדה status is known to her neighbors, it is established fact, and he can learn it from them.

steps.title: How does he find out she did not separate חלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a wife who does not separate חלה and asks the same question: if he knew, he should have stayed away; if he did not know, how did he find out?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and she does not separate חלה.' What is the case? If he knows, he should keep away from it. If he does not know, how does he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, חלה, and asks the same two-sided question it asked about the earlier cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he knew the dough had no חלה taken, he would be at fault for eating it. If he did not know, there seems to be no way for him to discover it later. Either way, it is unclear how this case leads to divorce without a כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates חלה, the portion of dough given to a כהן
What is the case? How does it work?

phrases.english: "Or she does not separate חלה."
What are the circumstances?
If he knows, let him keep away;
if he does not know, how does he know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same question as steps 20 and 22, now applied to the חלה case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a wife who does not separate חלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two-sided problem: if he knew, he is at fault himself; if he did not know, he has no way of finding out.

steps.title: She lied that a baker fixed the dough
steps.stepSummary: The case is where she told him a certain baker took חלה from the dough. He asked the baker and found out it was a lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where she told him: 'So-and-so the baker fixed the dough for me.' He went and asked him, and it turned out to be a lie.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in the same pattern as before. She named a specific person, he checked, and the lie came out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the answers about מעשר (step 21) and נדה (step 24). Her specific, checkable claim is what lets him find out afterward. She deceived him, so she loses her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed or prepared; here, took off the חלה

phrases.english: No, it is needed where she said to him:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלוֹנִי גַּבָּל תִּיקֵּן לִי אֶת הָעִיסָּה,
phrases.english: So-and-so the kneader fixed the dough for me,
phrases.notes: "Fixed" means he took off the חלה so the dough could be eaten.

phrases.english: and he went and asked him, and it turned out to be a lie.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאָמְרָה לֵיהּ: פְּלוֹנִי גַּבָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no way for him to find out about the חלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: She named a baker. He checked with the baker and found out it was a lie.
steps.whatToRemember: All three cases (מעשר, נדה, חלה) work the same way. The wife made a specific claim the husband could check, and checking it showed she lied.

steps.title: Why unkept vows matter: children die
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a wife who vows and does not keep her vows. It explains that for the sin of vows children die, learned from a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she vows and does not keep her vows.' As the Master said: for the sin of vows, children die, as it says: 'Do not let your mouth bring your flesh to sin...' (and it ends 'and destroy the work of your hands'). What is the work of a person's hands? You must say: his sons and daughters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and explains why it is a reason for divorce. A wife who breaks her vows brings danger to the family's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases the wife caused her husband to sin. Here only she sins, so the גמרא shows why it still affects him. The פסוק warns that broken vows lead to 'destroying the work of your hands,' and a person's 'handiwork' is explained as his children.

keyTerms.meaning: She makes vows and does not keep them

phrases.english: "Or she vows and does not fulfill."
As the Master said:
For the sin of vows, children die,
as it is said: "Do not let your mouth
bring your flesh to sin, etc."
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:5. The "etc." is pointing to the end of the פסוק: "and destroy the work of your hands."

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזוֹ הֵן מַעֲשֵׂה יָדָיו שֶׁל אָדָם —
phrases.english: And what is the work of a person's hands?
You must say: his sons and his daughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: בַּעֲוֹן נְדָרִים בָּנִים מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה and explains the reason behind it.
steps.raayaObject: Why a wife who breaks her vows can be sent away without a כתובה
steps.raayaSupportSource: קהלת 5:5, where "the work of your hands" means one's children
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the husband is harmed even though the sin is only hers: the punishment for broken vows falls on the children.

steps.title: רב נחמן's source: "In vain I struck your children"
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן brings a different פסוק from ירמיהו: 'In vain I struck your children.' 'In vain' means because of empty words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said it comes from here: 'In vain I struck your children.' 'In vain' means because of matters of empty words.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן offers a second פסוק as the source that children die because of unkept vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לשוא' (in vain) is read as 'because of שוא,' meaning empty words: vows that were never kept. So the פסוק itself links striking the children to broken vows.

keyTerms.meaning: In vain; read here as "because of empty words"
Matters of emptiness, meaning empty, unkept words

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: from here:
"In vain I struck your children";
"In vain" means: on account of matters of emptiness.
phrases.notes: "Emptiness" here means words that stayed empty: vows that were never kept.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same idea as step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That children die because of unkept vows
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 2:30, "לשוא" read as "because of empty words"

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the husband should make her vow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי מאיר says a man who knows his wife makes vows and does not keep them should 'go back and make her vow.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר used to say: anyone who knows that his wife vows and does not keep her vows should go back and make her vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's advice for a husband in this situation. Its wording is unclear, and the גמרא will question it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר seems to be offering a way to fix the problem without divorce. But the plain wording, 'make her vow,' sounds like it would make things worse. That sets up the גמרא's question.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say:
Anyone who knows about his wife
that she vows and does not fulfill,
should go back and make her vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical suggestion about the case of unkept vows discussed in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband whose wife breaks her vows should take some action ("make her vow") to deal with it.

steps.title: How would making her vow help?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled: how does making her take a vow fix anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: Make her vow?! How does that fix things for her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רבי מאיר's advice from step 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her problem is that she makes vows and breaks them. Giving her another vow only adds another chance to break one. So the plain reading cannot be right.

phrases.english: Make her vow?!
How is he fixing it for her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבי מאיר's statement in step 30.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding more vows would make her problem worse, not solve it.

steps.title: Rather: provoke her so he can cancel her vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי מאיר: the husband should provoke her so she vows in front of him, and then he can cancel the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: he should go back and provoke her, so that she vows in front of him and he can cancel it for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 31 by changing the wording of רבי מאיר's advice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has the power to cancel his wife's vows when he hears them. If he gets her to vow in his presence, he can cancel it right away. That way the vow is never left standing to be broken.

keyTerms.meaning: He should provoke or anger her

phrases.english: Rather: he should go back and provoke her,
so that she vows in front of him and he cancels it for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He should give her a new vow, which makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: He should get her to vow in front of him so he can cancel it on the spot.

steps.title: The Sages: no one lives with a snake in a basket
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי מאיר's idea: a person cannot live in a tight basket with a snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: a person does not live with a snake in a basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים respond to רבי מאיר and reject his solution as unrealistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His plan would mean constantly provoking his wife and watching over every vow she makes. Living like that is as dangerous and tense as sharing a small basket with a snake. So he cannot be expected to stay with her, and divorce is the better option.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה.
phrases.english: A person does not live with a snake in a basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים reject רבי מאיר's solution as explained in step 32.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי מאיר's practical solution of provoking her and cancelling her vows
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is unrealistic to expect a man to live in constant tension, always watching for her vows.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, a husband does not have to keep managing his wife's vows. She can be divorced, as the משנה says.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: The Husband Should Separate the חלה Himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה says a husband who knows his wife does not separate חלה should separate it himself after she finishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה used to say: Anyone who knows that his wife does not separate חלה for him should go back and separate it after her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that is built just like רבי מאיר's teaching about vows, but this one is about חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gave a way for the husband to fix his wife's vows. רבי יהודה gives the same kind of advice for חלה: the husband quietly separates it himself, so the bread is no longer forbidden. Either way, the husband fixes the problem himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough that must be separated and given to a כהן
He should go back and separate it himself
After her, once she is finished

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda used to say:
Anyone who knows about his wife
that she does not separate חלה for him
should go back and separate it after her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא to רבי מאיר's teaching (Step 30), applying the same idea to חלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who knows his wife does not separate חלה should separate it himself after her.

steps.title: The Sages Reject It: No One Lives with a Snake in a Basket
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה with the same reply they gave רבי מאיר: a person cannot live with a snake in a basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A person does not live together with a snake in a basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's advice using the very same image they used against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the husband cannot be expected to keep checking up on a wife who keeps doing wrong. Living with her is like living with a snake in a tight basket. So his fixing it does not solve the problem, and the marriage problem stays.

phrases.english: They said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה.
phrases.english: A person does not live with a snake in a basket.
phrases.notes: This is the same line the חכמים said to רבי מאיר in Step 33.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין אָדָם דָּר עִם נָחָשׁ בִּכְפִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's advice from Step 34.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the husband's fixing solves the problem with the wife.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A husband cannot be expected to keep watching over a wife who keeps doing wrong.

steps.title: Comparing the Two Cases: חלה and Vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the two teachings relate: whoever says the fix works for חלה would surely say it for vows, but someone who says it for vows may not say it for חלה, since the husband may end up eating untithed bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever teaches it about this case (חלה) would teach it all the more so about that case (vows). But whoever teaches it about that case (vows) would say: in this case (חלה), sometimes he happens to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two teachings it just brought and explains which case is easier to fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vows do not happen every day, so the husband can deal with them. חלה comes up all the time, so the husband cannot always catch it, and sometimes he will eat the bread before he separates the חלה. That is why the fix for vows does not prove a fix for חלה, but a fix for חלה surely proves one for vows.

keyTerms.meaning: About this one / about that one
Sometimes he happens to eat it

steps.whatToRemember: Fixing vows is easier than fixing חלה, because חלה comes up every day and the husband may eat the bread before he can fix it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אהא' (this) means חלה and 'אהך' (that) means vows. Keep track of which is which, or the whole line flips around.

phrases.english: Whoever teaches it about this,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the case of חלה, which we just learned.

phrases.english: all the more so about that.
phrases.notes: 'That' means the earlier case of vows.

phrases.english: But whoever teaches it about that (vows),
but this one (חלה) —
sometimes he happens to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא, כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן אַהָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the two parallel ברייתות by explaining how their cases relate.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whoever says the husband can fix it for חלה surely says so for vows, but not the other way around, because with חלה he may end up eating untithed bread.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: Going Out with an Uncovered Head
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's example of breaking דת יהודית: a woman who goes out with her head uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is דת יהודית? She goes out with her head uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's example of דת יהודית. It is setting up a question about this example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists actions that break 'Jewish custom' (דת יהודית), and the first one is going out with an uncovered head. By calling it 'custom', the משנה makes it sound like a custom and not a Torah law. The next step will question exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The practice of Jewish women (modest customs)

phrases.english: And what is Jewish practice?
She goes out with her head uncovered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the משנה's list of actions that break דת יהודית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman going out with her head uncovered breaks דת יהודית.

steps.title: But an Uncovered Head Is a Torah Law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: an uncovered head is forbidden by the Torah, as learned from the סוטה פסוק. So why does the משנה call it only 'Jewish practice'?
steps.simpleTranslation: An uncovered head is a Torah law, as it is written: 'And he shall uncover the head of the woman.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: This is a warning to Jewish women not to go out with an uncovered head!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: going out with an uncovered head is a Torah law, not just a custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן uncovers the head of a סוטה. דבי רבי ישמעאל learn from this that a woman's head is normally covered, so going out uncovered is forbidden by the Torah. If so, it should be listed under דת משה (Torah law), not דת יהודית (custom).

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
A warning (a source for a prohibition)

phrases.english: An uncovered head is a Torah law,
as it is written: 'And he shall uncover the head of the woman,'
and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
a warning to Jewish women
not to go out with an uncovered head!
phrases.notes: If the כהן has to uncover her head, that means it is normally covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's label from Step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of an uncovered head under דת יהודית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah source forbids an uncovered head, so it should be listed as Torah law, not custom.

steps.title: The Answer Begins: By Torah Law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer with the word 'By Torah law', and the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to answer the question. This step only opens the answer, which goes on at the top of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דאורייתא' shows the גמרא agrees that there is a Torah rule here. It is about to explain what exactly the Torah requires and what part is only Jewish custom.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (the opening of the answer)

phrases.english: By Torah law —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of Step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case into a Torah part and a custom part (continues on the next amud).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An uncovered head is entirely a Torah law, so it does not belong under דת יהודית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is only started here; the full answer comes next.
